transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, it's... it's mostly my sleep. Or, I guess, the fact that I'm not really sleeping at all anymore. I work as a personal care aide, you know, and I do these overnight shifts which are already hard enough on your body, but lately, it's just been impossible. I'll get off work, and I'll be so exhausted, like down to my bones, but I just lie there in bed. Wide awake. Staring at the ceiling. And my mind just won't turn off, no matter what I do. And then, if I finally do manage to drift off for a little bit, it's never peaceful. I wake up suddenly, and I'm just terrified... my heart is pounding, and I feel this awful sense of dread, like something terrible is happening or is going to happen. And even if I manage to stay in bed, when I finally get up for the day, I feel like I haven't slept a single minute. It's like the sleep doesn't even count. I'm just so drained all the time, and I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this, trying to take care of other people when I can't even get my own brain to let me rest for a few hours.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively worried or anxious most days, even when you're not trying to sleep?

No, I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person, really. I mean, not like... not like a worrywart or anything. It's just that when the sun goes down and I know I have to try to sleep, that's when it all starts. During the day, or, well, my day, which is usually the afternoon because of my shifts... I'm mostly just tired. So, so tired. I don't really have the energy to worry about things like paying bills or what I'm going to make for dinner or, I don't know, normal things people worry about. It's more like... I just feel this heavy, heavy weight on me all the time. But it's not worry. It's just... I don't know, it's just this feeling that everything is pointless and I'm just dragging myself from one minute to the next. Like, my clients, they need me to be alert and present, and I try, I really do, but it's like I'm moving through molasses. And I don't feel anxious about it, I just feel... empty. Just completely hollowed out. But no, not really worried. Just tired. Always so tired.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Well, I guess... yeah. I mean, it's not even just that I don't enjoy things, it's like I don't even remember how to. Most days, I wake up—if you can even call it waking up since I barely sleep—and I just feel this immense, crushing heaviness. It's like I'm wearing a lead suit before my feet even hit the floor. And there's just this emptiness inside me, right from the minute I open my eyes. I used to be so different, you know? I used to love going to church on Sundays, getting dressed up, seeing everybody, singing... I felt connected. And on Tuesdays and Thursdays, I'd go to this Zumba class at the community center. I wasn't great at it, but the music was loud and it felt good to just move and sweat and laugh with the other ladies. And I'd volunteer sometimes, helping out the kids at the after-school program, helping them with their homework or just playing games with them. I loved those kids. But now? Now I don't do any of it. I haven't been to church in months, I don't even know where my Zumba shoes are, and the thought of being around those kids just makes me feel exhausted and... and guilty, really, because I know I wouldn't have the energy to give them what they need. It's like that person—the one who did all those things and actually smiled and felt things—she's just completely gone. I look in the mirror and I don't even recognize the woman looking back at me, because she's just a hollow shell of who I used to be. Everything I used to love just feels like a chore now, a mountain I can't climb. So I just don't do anything besides work and lie in bed, feeling empty.
Have you been feeling this way — this heavy, empty, and without energy — every day for most of the day, and has it been going on for at least two weeks straight?

Two weeks? Oh, doctor, I wish it had only been two weeks. If it was just two weeks, maybe I could convince myself it was just a bad phase, you know? Like a bug I caught or something. No, it's been... it's been so much longer than that. It's been about a year and two months now. I know exactly when it started because it was right around the time my agency completely upended my schedule. 

They changed me to these rotating overnight shifts, which means one week I'm working Monday, Wednesday, Friday nights, and the next week it's Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and my body just never knows what time it is anymore. And on top of that, they added all this extra paperwork. It used to be you just cared for the client, made sure they were clean and fed and safe, and you wrote a little note at the end of the shift. But now, they want these detailed logs every two hours, documenting every single thing, and it's just... it's so much pressure when you're already exhausted and trying to stay awake at 3:00 AM. 

So, yeah, ever since they made those changes, about fourteen months ago, that's when this heavy feeling started creeping in. At first, I thought I just needed to adjust to the new schedule, you know? I told myself, 'Give it a month, your body will get used to it.' But it never did. It just got worse and worse, and that emptiness just settled into my chest and refused to leave. Every single day, for over a year now, I wake up feeling like I'm already defeated before the day even begins. It's not just a passing thing. It's my whole life now, every day, all day.
Have you ever felt so low or hopeless that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

I mean... yeah. I guess I do. I don't know if I'd say I sit around planning out how to hurt myself, like with a knife or anything like that, but... I think about dying. I think about it a lot, actually. 

It's always the absolute worst when I'm driving home in the morning after my shift. I get off around seven or eight, depending on how long that awful paperwork takes me, and the sun is usually just coming up. The light is always so bright, and I see all these other cars on the highway with people drinking their coffee, heading to their normal jobs, starting their normal days, and I'm just... I'm so completely drained. I'll be gripping the steering wheel, just staring at the road, and I just find myself wishing that I could go home, get in bed, and just not wake up. Just let that be the end of it. 

Or maybe just... disappear entirely. Like, just evaporate into thin air. Because honestly, doctor, I really feel like everybody would just be safer without me here. I look at my clients, and they're so vulnerable, you know? They rely on me to keep them safe and clean, and I'm just this hollowed-out ghost going through the motions. I feel like my presence is just... bad. Like I'm doing more harm than good just by being around them, and if I just vanished, they could get a better aide, someone who isn't so broken and empty. Everyone would just be safer, and so much better off, if I just wasn't around to mess things up or drag them down. 

So, yeah... on those drives home, watching the trees go by, the thought of just disappearing, of dying... it doesn't even scare me anymore. It feels more like a relief. It's just this constant loop in my head wishing I could just be gone.
